checks.title: Tickets matched to the stop sequence; fare grows with distance
checks.summary: Share of passengers whose boarding and alighting stops were matched to a route's stop order, and a check that fares rise with GTFS distance.

checks.title: Predicting a week the model has not seen
checks.summary: Leave-one-week-out on weekdays (test weeks 1-4). Prior, prior strength and range calibration are re-fit without the test week.

metrics.weekends: reported separately in outputs/eval/summary.json; one day per week so folds are low-power

checks.title: Matches known patterns: peaks, weekends, hubs
checks.summary: Bus-minute-weighted mean load on weekdays, weekday vs weekend ticket volume per day, and the busiest boarding areas (stops grouped within ~400 m). The pass criterion covers the peak and weekend ratios; the hub list is reported as-is.

checks.title: Plausibility and sensitivity
checks.summary: No independent on-board counts exist, so these are plausibility checks, not accuracy. Absolute headcounts depend on the scale factor and capacity cap below.

metrics.back-of-envelope load factor (inputs unv: about 20 riders per bus from ~630 boardings/bus-day x ~7 km / ~210 bus-km/day; fleet size, trip length and speed must be confirmed before quoting
metrics.city ridership implied after the cap vs: 54%  (ticket capture is clearly not uniform across routes)
metrics.not run: alighting-kernel on/off, 30 vs 60 minute bins, timestamp +/-5 min: require re-running the credits stage

checks.title: Journey planner behaves as specified
checks.summary: Nine origin-destination pairs including one needing a change. Checks: distinct buses, requested departure never dropped, time-shifted options only if strictly better crowding, sane times.

checks.title: Blind spots and the per-trip running count
checks.summary: Where the estimate is weakest, and the brief's per-trip running count as a diagnostic (tickets per vehicle-day are too few for it to be the main method).
